title: Blockading a passed pawn

D0.outcome: Explains blockading as placing a supported piece on the square in front of a passed pawn so it cannot advance and its own pieces stay cramped.

D1.outcome: Chooses the blockading square and piece (a knight is the best default) for a given passed pawn.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, decides among blockading, watching from a distance or attacking the pawn, and supports the blockader.

D3.outcome: Predicts how the blockader's quality and elasticity change the plan, and when to exchange a strong blockader for a weaker one; knows a far-advanced passer may be better watched.

misconceptions: The blockade is obligatory for every passed pawn.
Blockade with whichever piece is nearest.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.1.md §3 (POS.BLOCKADE: a default, not a duty)
conditions: The blockading piece is well supported; the pawn is dangerous or central.
Minor pieces make the best blockaders; the queen leaves at the first attack; the king is poor in the middlegame and useful in the endgame.
contrasts: A queen or king blockader that is exposed to attack.
'the blockade is obligatory' overreaches; a far-advanced passer may be better watched and a blockader can be overloaded.
A passed pawn that is already harmless.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.WEAKSQ.D2: the blockading square is a weak square for the pawn's owner
